identity.title: Recovering the gas properties of protoplanetary disks through parametric visibility modeling: MHO 6

paper_type_evidence.quote: we have introduced a parametric model to fit the main observable properties of the gaseous disk component in the visibility plane
The dataset was obtained by ALMA in Band 7, as part of the project 2018.1.00310.S (PI: P. Pinilla).

evidence.quote: located in the Taurus star-forming region at 154 pc (cite: gaia2021edr3)
located in the Taurus star-forming region at 154 pc (cite: gaia2021edr3)

question.value: Can parametric visibility modeling of CO isotopologue line emission recover the gas properties (emission height, brightness temperature, stellar mass, geometry, disk size) of the compact disk around the very-low-mass star MHO 6, where image-based techniques struggle?

evidence.quote: we explore the advantages and limitations of describing the properties of the gas surface-emitting layer with a parametric visibility-based modeling.
For these reasons, we chose to describe the disk morphology directly in the visibilities.
The dataset was obtained by ALMA in Band 7, as part of the project 2018.1.00310.S (PI: P. Pinilla).
This work includes 0.87 mm observations of the disk around MHO 6.
The dataset was obtained by ALMA in Band 7, as part of the project 2018.1.00310.S (PI: P. Pinilla).

validation.value: Flux conservation of nested models compared with an n=6 reference over n=0..6 and 256 disk-center offsets

claims.hypothesis: Parametric visibility modeling can recover the stellar mass, geometry and central velocity of a compact disk from moderate-resolution CO data
claims.experiment: Independent MCMC fits of 12CO and 13CO J=3-2 visibilities of MHO 6
claims.result: 12CO gives M_star=0.164+/-0.003 Msun and 13CO gives 0.171 Msun; geometry and VLSR consistent between lines
claims.finding: The method returns consistent, literature-matching parameters even for the faint 13CO

evidence.quote: the models return the same consistent results for the stellar mass, disk geometry, and central velocity

claims.hypothesis: The emitting surface of a disk around a very-low-mass star is more elevated than around higher-mass stars
claims.experiment: Compare modeled z(r) of MHO 6 with the Law et al. sample using the same functional form
claims.result: MHO 6 is among the most elevated surfaces within the first 50 au, with z/r above 0.3 for 12CO out to 100 au
claims.finding: Consistent with models predicting geometrically thicker disks around very-low-mass stars

evidence.loc: 4.2 Comparison of MHO6 with other sources
evidence.quote: MHO 6 is among the most elevated emitting surfaces in both CO isotopologues when measured in distance from the midplane.

claims.hypothesis: The model can separate front and back layers to give brightness temperatures
claims.experiment: Convert model intensity of each layer to Rayleigh-Jeans brightness temperature
claims.result: Back-layer 12CO temperature of 18+/-1 K within 100 au
claims.finding: Consistent with CO freeze-out and a cold midplane with T<20 K

evidence.loc: 5.1 Morphology of MHO6 CO isotopologues emission
evidence.quote: This unprecedented measurement from a moderate resolution and moderate sensitivity observation suggests a cold midplane with $T<20$ K.

claims.hypothesis: A nested-image oversampling of the inner disk keeps flux fidelity without prohibitive pixel size

how_they_decided_enough.value: Nesting level chosen so that flux loss is below single-channel sensitivity

evidence.quote: The acceptable flux loss should be decided on the basis of a comparison with an observation’s sensitivity, such that the dominant uncertainty source is the single channel sensitivity and not the model’s flux loss.

limitations_admitted.value: Model ignores midplane absorption of back-layer emission, which could lower the observed brightness temperature

evidence.loc: 5.1 Morphology of MHO6 CO isotopologues emission

limitations_admitted.value: Brightness temperature highly uncertain inside 10 au

limitations_admitted.value: Spatial masking is not possible in visibility modeling

evidence.loc: 5.3 Advantages of image- versus visibility-based analysis
evidence.quote: Masking spatial regions is not possible with visibility modeling.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single source and single dataset; no injection-recovery test of the visibility model on synthetic data with known parameters
Optical depth of 12CO is assumed fully thick, so brightness temperatures are lower limits on kinetic temperature
Front and back layer heights forced equal; the 13CO turnover parameters are unconstrained
Likelihood and noise treatment are not described

evidence.quote: for making them available for public use
